To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) a system that uses only a simple keyword matching algorithm can answer a substantial fraction of the questions in the TREC-8 question answering test collection; (b) the addition of a simple question classifier can improve performance significantly; (c) a simple question classifier is sufficient to predict the likelihood that a given answer is correct, and this likelihood can then be used to rank answers.

(1) a system that relies on data redundancy and a simple question classifier can outperform systems that rely on sophisticated linguistic analyses, (2) the system can be made more robust to incorrect answers by predicting when the system will fail and by using the prediction to select a different answer, (3) the system is most likely to fail when the question is about a specific fact, and (4) the system is more likely to succeed when the question is a yes-no question.
